# eslint-plugin-lambda-security

Guide for AI coding assistants using this plugin in a project. To change the plugin's own source, read https://github.com/ofri-peretz/eslint/blob/main/AGENTS.md instead.

> ESLint Lambda security rules for AWS Lambda — detects overly permissive IAM policies and CORS, unvalidated event bodies, secrets in env vars, and leaked error details.

## Enable it

```bash
npm install --save-dev eslint-plugin-lambda-security
```

Requires ESLint ^8.40.0 || ^9.0.0 || ^10.0.0 and Node >=22.13.0.

```js
// eslint.config.mjs
import lambdaSecurity from 'eslint-plugin-lambda-security';

export default [lambdaSecurity.configs.recommended];
```

Each preset is one flat config object: put it in the array as an element, do not spread it. Rule ids are prefixed `lambda-security/`. Add it to the config you already have; do not remove other plugins. TypeScript files need a TypeScript parser in the config (`typescript-eslint`).

Use it alongside `eslint-plugin-security`, not instead of it: keep that plugin if the project has it. Measured overlap and the limits of both: https://eslint.interlace.tools/docs/getting-started/with-eslint-plugin-security

## Presets

| Preset        | Rules | Errors | Warnings |
| ------------- | ----- | ------ | -------- |
| `recommended` | 14    | 7      | 7        |
| `strict`      | 14    | 14     | 0        |

### `recommended`

14 rules:

- `no-hardcoded-credentials-sdk` (error): Detects hardcoded AWS credentials in SDK client configurations.
- `no-permissive-cors-response` (error): Detects permissive CORS (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *) in Lambda response headers.
- `no-permissive-cors-middy` (error): Detects @middy/http-cors middleware with permissive origin (*).
- `no-secrets-in-env` (error): Detects secrets directly assigned to environment variables.
- `no-user-controlled-requests` (error): Detects HTTP requests with user-controlled URLs (SSRF vulnerability).
- `no-overly-permissive-iam-policy` (error): Detects IAM policies with overly broad permissions (wildcards).
- `no-unvalidated-event-body` (warn): Detects Lambda handlers using event body/params without validation.
- `no-missing-authorization-check` (warn): Detects Lambda handlers without authorization checks.
- `no-exposed-error-details` (warn): Detects Lambda handlers exposing internal error details in responses.
- `no-exposed-debug-endpoints` (error): Detect debug endpoints without auth in AWS Lambda handlers.
- `no-env-logging` (warn): Detects logging of process.env which may expose secrets.
- `no-error-swallowing` (warn): Detects empty catch blocks and missing error logging in Lambda handlers.
- `require-timeout-handling` (warn): Warns when Lambda handlers with external calls lack timeout handling.
- `no-unbounded-batch-processing` (warn): Detects processing batch records without size validation.

### `strict`

Same rules as `recommended`.

## Other Interlace plugins by dependency

If the project also depends on one of these, add the matching plugin the same way:

- `express`, `fastify`, `koa`, `@hapi/hapi`, `restify`, `hono`, `next`, `@nestjs/core`, `@nestjs/common`, `aws-lambda`, `@types/aws-lambda`, `@middy/core`, `commander`, `yargs`, `@oclif/core`, `@modelcontextprotocol/*`: `eslint-plugin-node-security`
- `express`: `eslint-plugin-express-security`
- `@nestjs/common`, `@nestjs/core`: `eslint-plugin-nestjs-security`
- `react`, `react-dom`, `preact`, `vue`, `svelte`, `@angular/core`, `solid-js`, `lit`, `next`, `nuxt`: `eslint-plugin-browser-security`
- `jsonwebtoken`, `jose`, `express-jwt`, `@nestjs/jwt`, `jwks-rsa`, `jwt-decode`: `eslint-plugin-jwt-security`
- `pg`, `pg-pool`, `pg-promise`, `postgres`, `slonik`: `eslint-plugin-postgresql-security`
- `mysql2`, `mysql`: `eslint-plugin-mysql-security`
- `mongodb`, `mongoose`: `eslint-plugin-mongodb-security`
- `better-sqlite3`, `sqlite3`: `eslint-plugin-sqlite-security`
- `knex`: `eslint-plugin-knex-security`
- `@prisma/client`, `prisma`: `eslint-plugin-prisma-security`
- `drizzle-orm`: `eslint-plugin-drizzle-security`
- `sequelize`: `eslint-plugin-sequelize-security`
- `typeorm`: `eslint-plugin-typeorm-security`
- `@supabase/supabase-js`: `eslint-plugin-supabase-security`
- `@modelcontextprotocol/*`: `eslint-plugin-mcp-sdk-security`
- `openai`, `@openai/agents`: `eslint-plugin-openai-security`
- `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`: `eslint-plugin-anthropic-security`
- `@google/genai`: `eslint-plugin-gemini-security`
- `ai`: `eslint-plugin-vercel-ai-security`

The full stack-to-plugin playbook (with config rendering and a proof step) is the `security-linting` skill: https://github.com/ofri-peretz/eslint/tree/main/skills/security-linting
